extracted.intended_audience: licensing professionals, patent litigators, damages experts, and economists who determine reasonable royalty rates in patent disputes
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and determining a reasonable royalty rate for patent infringement using the Georgia‑Pacific hypothetical negotiation framework, with emphasis on how industry norms and observed license agreement rates inform that analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothetical negotiation construct
rubrics_metrics.description: Georgia‑Pacific contemplates that parties to infringement litigation engage in a hypothetical negotiation assumed to occur just prior to the date of alleged infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hypothetical negotiation is intended to produce a license agreement similar to what a willing licensor and willing licensee would have agreed to, neither under any compulsion to enter into an agreement, assuming the patents in question were understood to be valid and infringed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of the 15 Georgia‑Pacific factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with Georgia‑Pacific, the parties may consider 15 factors, among other things, in connection with their negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of these factors (often called a Georgia‑Pacific analysis) is intended to produce damages “adequate to compensate” the patent holder for infringement; the factors should be evaluated collectively in the hypothetical negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry royalty rates as evidence (Georgia‑Pacific factor 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Georgia‑Pacific factor 12: “the portion of profit or selling price that may be customary in the particular business or in comparable businesses to allow for the use of the inventions or analogous inventions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This calls for an evaluation of royalty rates paid for licenses to technology in the relevant industry; observed industry average royalty rates often are considered as part of the analysis and determination of a reasonable royalty rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of empirical studies of industry license agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical study of industry license agreements can provide observed industry average royalty rates that inform the hypothetical negotiation construct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results from such studies provide useful context within which rates for specific patent claims can be assessed, but they are contextual evidence rather than determinative on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of established royalties for the specific technology (Georgia‑Pacific factors 1 and 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The results from industry studies are not intended to serve as a substitute for analysis of Georgia‑Pacific factors 1 and 2, which relate to established royalties for the specific technology in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts must separately evaluate past established royalties and licensing practices specific to the patented technology and incorporate those findings into the hypothetical negotiation rather than relying solely on industry averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of producing an adequate compensatory royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of the Georgia‑Pacific analysis is intended to provide damages “adequate to compensate” the patent holder for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All factors and evidence (including industry norms) should be used to model a license that a willing licensor and willing licensee would have struck under the stated assumptions; credibility of comparables and assumptions about validity/infringement are central.
